protocol: 3 rounds x 3 proposals; one positive scoring winner at most per round

descriptor_candidates.name: confined_free_volume_entropy
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Adsorption entropy loss scales with the ratio of pore (framework) accessible volume to adsorbate molecular volume, corrected by pore-to-free-diameter confinement ratio; the log-volume-ratio term dominates in large-pore regimes while the diameter-ratio term dominates in narrow-pore confinement.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: configurational restriction of a molecule in a cavity depends on the free-volume fraction and on how tightly the pore diameter (lsd_p) compresses the diffusive free path (lsd_f). A tighter lsd_p/lsd_f ratio means stronger translational constraint, larger entropy loss.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this descriptor as a 15th input to the full 14-input network does not reduce MAE of entropy loss/R relative to the 14-input baseline across repeated cross-validation splits, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_anisotropy_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with adsorbate shape anisotropy (PMI3/PMI1) multiplied by a shape-compactness factor (PBF/SPAN) and framework packing density: elongated, anisotropic molecules in densely packed frameworks lose more rotational/translational entropy upon adsorption.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: highly anisotropic molecules (large PMI3/PMI1) have orientation-dependent confinement; PBF/SPAN penalizes protruding shapes; source-scale density proxies framework atom packing, which restricts orientational freedom. Their product captures shape-framework compatibility effects on adsorbed-state entropy.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor shows no rank correlation improvement in residuals of the baseline network (e.g., |Spearman rho| of descriptor vs. baseline residuals < 0.2 or no MAE reduction when appended), the shape-anisotropy mechanism is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_access_per_mass
descriptor_candidates.formula: log((LabuteASA * MW) / (ASA * Vol + 1.0)) + (AV / (AV + lsd_f * lsd_f * lsd_f))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss correlates with the mismatch between molecular exposed surface per volume and framework gravimetric surface area, saturating at high accessible pore volume per free-diameter cube: adsorbates whose LabuteASA/Vol exceeds the framework's surface-to-pore ratio experience proportionally stronger entropy loss.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: when a molecule's surface-area-to-volume ratio is large relative to the framework's available surface per pore volume, a larger fraction of the molecule contacts pore walls, removing rotational and vibrational freedom; the AV saturation term captures diminishing returns in very open frameworks. Density is deliberately excluded to avoid unverified unit interpretation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's partial contribution (permutation importance or ablation MAE change) is not statistically significant (e.g., paired t-test p > 0.05 on CV folds) versus the 14-input baseline, the surface-mismatch hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_tightness_moment
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows when the adsorbate volume-to-framework-accessible-volume ratio is high, when the molecule protrudes deeply into the pore relative to pore diameter, and when framework packing density (source scale) is high relative to molecular mass; all three factors jointly reduce translational and rotational freedom of the adsorbed phase.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: Vol/(AV+1) measures how much of the accessible pore volume a single molecule occupies; PBF/lsd_p compares molecular protruding depth with pore size, penalizing tight wall contact; the log density-mass contrast encodes framework packing on the native scale without asserting units. Inference from confinement theory, not from a retrieved source.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Appending this descriptor to the 14-input network must reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5449 (the round-1 best) on repeated CV splits; if the median MAE is not reduced, the packing-tightness mechanism is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: asphericity_pore_geometry
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Molecules with large asphericity (geometric-mean large principal moments over the smallest) confined in pores whose free diameter exceeds the pore-limiting diameter lose more rotational entropy; the SPAN/GeDi contrast adds a linear-extent-to-diameter mismatch term that further predicts entropy loss for rod-like adsorbates.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: rotational entropy loss upon adsorption depends on how anisotropic the inertia-like geometry is and on how anisotropic the pore channel is (lsd_f vs lsd_p); elongated molecules in channel-like pores retain translational freedom along one axis but lose two rotational degrees, which this product captures. Inference, no source evidence.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If permuting this descriptor yields no significant MAE increase (paired t-test p > 0.05 across CV folds) versus the retained baseline network, the asphericity-pore-geometry mechanism is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: gravimetric_surface_saturation
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with framework gravimetric surface area scaled by packing density per molecular mass, is moderated by the molecule's own surface-to-volume ratio (saturating contact term), and grows linearly with accessible pore volume per free diffusion diameter; the combination predicts that large, open frameworks adsorb with the least entropy loss only when molecular contact area is also small.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: ASA*density/MW proxies framework surface available per molecular amount; exp(-LabuteASA/Vol) is a saturating molecular-contact penalty whose minimum (approaching 0 for large surface-to-volume molecules) deepens the descriptor; AV/lsd_f is a channel-efficiency term. Distinguishes wall-contact effects from free-volume effects. Inference from Henry-law adsorption thermodynamics intuition (known in spirit but combined newly).
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Ablating this descriptor must increase MAE of entropy loss/R significantly relative to the 15-input network containing the retained descriptor; if removal changes MAE by less than 0.005 with p > 0.05 across folds, the surface-saturation hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: vibrational_tightness_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases when the adsorbate is heavy relative to framework packing density (lower vibrational frequencies in the adsorbed state), when the molecule is compact for its surface (Vol/LabuteASA high, weaker wall coupling), and when the molecule occupies a large fraction of the pore-limiting volume (lsd_p^3), all jointly suppressing vibrational freedom upon adsorption.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference, no source evidence): adsorbed-phase vibrational entropy scales inversely with molecular mass and with confinement stiffness; a compact molecule in a pore whose limiting cube volume is comparable to its molecular volume experiences the stiffest wall potential. The sqrt mass-density term uses the source density scale without asserting units. Expected regime: small-to-medium molecules in narrow-pore zeolites.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Appending this descriptor to the 14-input network must reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5449 on repeated CV splits; if the median MAE across folds is not reduced (paired test p > 0.05), the vibrational-tightness mechanism is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: aspect_ratio_channel_lock
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is largest when the molecule's longest linear dimension (SPAN) nearly matches the smaller of the two pore diameters (interpolative minimum locks the molecule in the channel) AND the intermediate-to-smallest principal-moment ratio is large (intermediate-axis orientation is constrained); the GeDi/SPAN log term adds a correction for gyration-diameter compactness of near-spherical adsorbates, which should weaken the lock effect.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from configurational-integral confinement reasoning): when a molecular dimension approaches the critical pore diameter, translation along all axes is suppressed (window-passing entropy cost); this cost is orientation-dependent and scales with intermediate-axis asymmetry. Expected regime: elongated molecules in small-pore zeolites with lsd_p close to SPAN. Distinct from prior descriptors because it uses a minimum operator to select the binding pore dimension rather than ratios of accessible volumes or surface areas.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's partial correlation with baseline-network residuals has |Spearman rho| < 0.2, or appending it does not reduce median CV MAE of entropy loss/R relative to 0.5449 with significance (paired t-test p <= 0.05), the channel-lock mechanism is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: diametric_exclusion_fraction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss decreases exponentially with the ratio of pore-limiting diameter to molecular gyration diameter (near-free translational retention when GeDi >> lsd_p), but increases with the framework's surface-area-per-mass-times-pore-volume content and with molecular protrusion (PBF/SPAN) in densely packed frameworks; net entropy loss is the balance of an exclusion penalty and a wall-contact gain.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference): exp(-lsd_p/GeDi) is a smooth exclusion fraction — molecules much larger than the limiting window lose near-full translational entropy (term near 0), small molecules retain it (term near 1), so entropy loss scales with 1 minus this fraction through the additive structure. ASA*AV/MW is framework wall availability per molecular amount; density/density+1 is a saturating packing factor on the source scale. Expected regime: broad, but exclusion term should dominate for sub-window-sized adsorbates.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Ablation of this descriptor from a 15-input network (14 inputs + retained descriptor + this one) must increase MAE of entropy loss/R by more than 0.005 with paired t-test p <= 0.05 across CV folds; otherwise the diametric-exclusion mechanism is falsified.
